name: Avoid Programs with High Fan-In (z/OS Assembler)
description:
Avoid Programs with High Fan-In (Fan-In > X). The Fan-In of an Artifact is the number of other Artifacts that are referencing it. When computing the Fan-In of an Artifact, multiple accesses to it from the same Artifact are counted as one access.
The threshold level is a parameter that can be changed at will.
For a z/OS Assembler Program, these Artifacts are the other z/OS Assembler Programs and Macros that call it with CALL or name it in PROGRAM('...'). The calls from the Programs of another analysis unit reach it through the Call to Generic Program object of that unit, which counts once whatever the number of callers. A COBOL program calling it through a COBOL program prototype does not count, the prototype not being an Artifact of the application.
output:
Associated to each z/OS Assembler Program with violations, the Quality Rule provides:
- The Fan-In
rationale:
An Artifact referenced by many other Artifacts is costly to change: a change can impact all of them, and all of them have to be tested again.
Changeability and testability decline with increasing Fan-In.
remediation: Review the design of the Program: split it into smaller Programs with a single responsibility each, so that each caller depends only on what it uses.
alternativeName: Avoid Programs with High Fan-In (z/OS Assembler)
